Session · What happened (August 17)
The session focused on refining the architecture and capabilities of the Team Intelligence Agent, particularly its interaction with knowledge bases and the overall system design for retrieval and evaluation. There was also a practical demonstration and discussion on deploying a Qdrant cluster for vector storage.

Technical concepts discussed
- **Team Intelligence Agent Capabilities**: Discussion centered on defining "intelligence" for the agent, moving beyond simple RAG to inferring patterns, evaluating projects, and generating comprehensive reports (e.g., 3000-token reports) by analyzing transcripts and knowledge bases. The agent should extract thinking patterns and answering patterns [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Knowledge Base Design**: The concept of a knowledge base was explored, with an emphasis on extracting entities like people, roles, tasks, projects, decisions, assignments, terminology, events, and facts. The knowledge base should include a "training profile" for each team member, updated daily, containing name, thinking style, assigned tasks, and evaluation scores [17 August 2026, Page 1-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **System Architecture for RAG**: A three-system architecture was outlined for the RAG pipeline:
    1.  **Vector Store System**: Handles parsing, cleaning, semantic chunking, embedding generation, and vector storage (e.g., Qdrant) [17 August 2026, Page 7-8 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 4 — Dakshinya Nachimuthu].
    2.  **Main RAG/Retrieval Service**: Contains different retrieval strategies (Experiment 1, 2, 3, 4), a prompt builder, context engineering engine, and a reusable reranker module [17 August 2026, Page 7-9 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 4 — Dakshinya Nachimuthu].
    3.  **Unified Evaluation System**: Handles evaluation metrics, separate from the retrieval experiments [17 August 2026, Page 7-9 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 4 — Dakshinya Nachimuthu].
- **Deployment with Qdrant Cloud**: A practical walkthrough of creating a free Qdrant cluster, obtaining API keys and endpoints, and the importance of selecting a region close to consumers was conducted [17 August 2026, Page 14-16 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Context and Prompt Engineering**: Emphasized the importance of designing the system from "harness first, then context, then prompt" and having separate Python files for context engineering and a prompt builder service to avoid hardcoding prompts [17 August 2026, Page 9-10 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Normalization Layer**: The need for a generic normalization solution that can identify patterns in transcripts using LLMs rather than hardcoded rules was highlighted [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Assignments and actions
- **System Owner**:
    - **Refine Team Intelligence Agent Capabilities**: Rework the capabilities of the Team Intelligence Agent to align with the definition of "intelligence" discussed, focusing on inferring patterns and generating comprehensive reports. This includes locking down the agent's persona and defining a set of rules [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Design Knowledge Base (V1)**: Develop a V1 design for the knowledge base, including a JSON schema for a "training profile" that stores facts and observable events for each team member. This profile should be updated daily and include name, thinking style, assigned tasks, and evaluation scores [17 August 2026, Page 2-4 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 17 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Build Mentor and Manager Agents**: Focus on building working versions of the mentor and manager agents, ensuring proper tool calls and defining their roles and personas. These should be demonstrated with logs [17 August 2026, Page 13-14 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 6 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Connect to GitHub MCP**: Ensure the Team Intelligence Agent can connect to GitHub MCP using tokens from all team members to read code and information [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Generic Normalizer**: Develop a generic normalization solution that uses LLMs to identify patterns in transcripts and transform them, rather than relying on hardcoded patterns. Evaluate its performance on today's morning transcript [17 August 2026, Page 1 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Dakshinya Nachimuthu**:
    - **Refactor RAG Pipeline into Three Services**: Transform the existing RAG pipeline into three distinct Fast API services: one for putting data into Qdrant, one for retrieval (with parameters for experiments and reranker on/off), and one for evaluation. This involves modularizing the code for reusability [17 August 2026, Page 4-5 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 9-11 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Implement Error Handling and Logging**: Incorporate proper error handling, callbacks, and comprehensive logging (using normal Python logger) within the LLM generation client and across all system components [17 August 2026, Page 5-6 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 8-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Separate Context and Prompt Engineering**: Create separate Python files for context engineering and a prompt builder service to manage prompts outside of hardcoded files [17 August 2026, Page 9-10 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Deploy Qdrant Cluster**: Successfully create and connect to a Qdrant cloud cluster, and smoke test the connection using a Python script to move existing collections [17 August 2026, Page 14-17 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Ganesh Krishna**:
    - **Update Ingestion Pipeline**: Change the ingestion pipeline to read from a database (DB) instead of directly from documents, after the normalization layer is deployed. This change should be implemented after the system design is finalized [17 August 2026, Page 11-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    - **Deploy Normalization Layer**: Deploy the normalization code as a service so other team members can consume normalized transcripts [17 August 2026, Page 12 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Team-Wide Action**:
    - **Create Shared GitHub Repo**: Create a shared GitHub repository for documents, which will serve as the source for transcripts instead of MCP [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Decisions
- **RAG Architecture**: The RAG pipeline will be structured into three distinct systems: Vector Store, Main RAG/Retrieval Service, and Unified Evaluation System [17 August 2026, Page 7-8 — Siddharth Saminathan; 17 August 2026, Page 4 — Dakshinya Nachimuthu].
- **Knowledge Base Structure**: The knowledge base will incorporate a "training profile" for each team member, updated daily, to track their progress and contributions [17 August 2026, Page 2-3 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Transcript Source**: A shared GitHub repository will be used for storing documents and transcripts, replacing direct MCP connection for this purpose [17 August 2026, Page 12-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Configuration File Format**: Configuration files can be in any format (JSON, YAML, XML, TXT), not exclusively YAML [17 August 2026, Page 16 — Siddharth Saminathan].

Important changes
- **Data Ingestion Source**: The ingestion pipeline for the RAG system will shift from reading directly from documents to reading from a shared database (DB) [17 August 2026, Page 11-13 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Reranker as a Separate Module**: The reranker component within the RAG system needs to be made a separate, reusable module to allow for flexible integration across different experiments [17 August 2026, Page 8-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
- **Prompt Management**: Prompts will no longer be hardcoded but managed through a separate prompt builder service [17 August 2026, Page 9-10 — Siddharth Saminathan].

What you need to know or do
As the System Owner, your immediate focus is to refine the capabilities of the Team Intelligence Agent, ensuring it can infer patterns and generate detailed reports. You need to design the V1 knowledge base, including a JSON schema for the "training profile" that tracks team member progress. Additionally, you must build and demonstrate working mentor and manager agents with proper tool calls and logging. Ensure the Team Intelligence Agent can connect to GitHub MCP using team tokens. Finally, develop a generic normalization solution for transcripts using LLMs and evaluate its effectiveness. You should also be aware of the new three-system RAG architecture and the shift to a shared DB for data ingestion.
